column7: Three Community Health Workers (CHWs) served at this aid post before it was closed. According to one source from Aiyari, the last CHW served here around 1979, and the aid post was closed around that year due to distance and the tough environment.

Aiyari's old airstrip was cleared in the early 1990s. Cone markers were put in place for landing, but no landing ever took place. Around 1993, one flight circled above the airstrip but never made its first landing. Airstrip is not in operation.

# Zone 4: Aiyari: Aiyari old Elementary & Community School site
column7: No Elementary or Community School buildings can be seen here today. This is now the old site for both schools. At the beginning of 2025, when the Community School was relocated to Jaure, the Elementary School also stopped holding classes up till now.

The old Aiyari village was relocated to its current site in the early 1990s. According to one account, the move began when a community member started gardening near the new site. As he settled there and continued his gardening away from the old village, others gradually followed him, and soon the new Aiyari village was formed. Another account states that the community relocated to the current site because of a land dispute.

According to two sources from Aiyari and Suari, this site is where the old aid post was built during colonial times and was run by white people. The dates when it was established and when it closed are unknown to both sources.
